steps.title: A request enters the engine
steps.detail: The server has already unpacked the HTTP body. What the engine sees is a URL, a provider string and the client's wishes about the target format.

steps.title: Resolve the provider string
steps.detail: Every provider has several accepted spellings — youtube, youtube.com, www.youtube.com — collected in VALID<NAME>NAMES and registered in SUPPORTEDPROVIDERS.

steps.title: Look up the function
steps.detail: Two separate mappings. Not every provider is in both: Default and wcoflix can be resolved but not searched. ProviderTypes also declares Aniworld, Dailymotion and ERROR, which are in neither mapping — the enum value exists but resolving one fails here. Filmpalast is in both, but its resolver is not finished and returns nothing.

branches.label: enum has no mapping entry → TaskFailedError

steps.title: validateHostPro
steps.detail:
The first thing every provider does. It pins the request to a fixed list of hostnames and usually to https. This is the SSRF guard: without it a crafted URL could make the server fetch anything on the local network.

Any new provider must do the same — it is a convention, not something the framework enforces.

steps.title: Find the real media URLs
steps.sub: three patterns, one per provider family
steps.detail:
How the provider gets there is entirely up to it, and this is where the time goes.

HTML regex (Bandcamp, Newgrounds, Suno, wcoflix): load the page, pull embedded stream URLs out of it. Browser sniffing (Soundcloud, YoutubeMusic, Default, Filmpalast): drive Chromium and record media responses — see the Browser sniffing flow. API (Youtube, Archive): the YouTube player API, tried with several client identities, or the Archive API hands back a format list.

The result is a list of FoundMedia. A candidate can carry a separate audio_url, which YouTube now does for its best video/audio pair.

steps.title: Score the candidates
steps.detail:
Extension priority, good and bad URL keywords and the client's wishes are added up, highest total wins. See the Picking a URL flow for the individual terms.

Afterwards the winner is measured: one small Range: bytes=0-0 request per URL tells the engine the size of the video and, if separate, the audio.

steps.title: Build the DownloadContext
steps.detail: One context per file. From here on this single object travels through every layer, and the downloaders write their progress straight into download_progress on it. The target holds the resolved URL, the optional audio_url and both sizes; the output holds the file name and whether auto_convert was requested.

steps.title: _splitContext
steps.detail: The dispatcher makes three copies of the DownloadInformation, each with only the contexts of one type. Which mechanism runs depends solely on target.download_type — not on the file extension and not on the provider.

steps.title: FILE: one URL, one range
steps.detail: One or two URLs, fetched in 10 MiB ranges up to the measured size by asyncDownloadYieldRanges(). With a separate audio URL there are two sources.

steps.title: HLS: playlist then segments
steps.detail: Two stages, detailed in the HLS download flow.

steps.title: UMP: stateful byte protocol
steps.detail: Google's container format behind googlevideo.com, detailed in the UMP / SABR flow. The youtube mode skips the codec check: yt-dlp merges on its own.

steps.title: Codec check: copy or mux?
steps.detail:
The first chunks of each source are piped into ffprobe until the codecs are known. If there is a single source, the target container is the one that was found and every codec is allowed in it, the bytes are passed through untouched.

Otherwise AsyncFFmpegMuxer starts ffmpeg with one input pipe per source, copies what the container accepts and re-encodes the rest. With auto_convert the target container is preferred_file instead of the found one, which is how a download arrives already converted.

steps.title: File on disk, or an async byte stream
steps.detail:
The base class builds both from the two methods every dispatcher implements. downloadToFile() runs all contexts in parallel through asyncio.gather; downloadAndYield() runs them one after another into a single stream; DownloadDispatcher.downloadContextAndYield() streams exactly one context, which is what the server uses.

Progress is written to the same DownloadProgress object in all three mechanisms, which is why the server's polling endpoint needs no state of its own.

steps.title: Dropped without an exception
steps.detail: A context whose type is not one of the three is marked FAILED in _splitContext() and quietly left out. Nothing is raised, so the caller sees a job that simply produced fewer files than it asked for. The reason is only in download_progress.error_message.

steps.title: TaskFailedError
steps.detail: The project's carrier for „this could not be done and here is what to try“. extraMessages is a list of hints that ends up in the message the user sees. The server turns it into a 500, and DRMProtectedMediaError into a 422. The ffmpeg layer adds FFmpegNotFoundError and FFmpegHttpError.

steps.title: A list of FoundMedia arrives
steps.detail: What the provider found. Browser providers pass content type and size from the response headers along; the YouTube provider passes extension, MIME type, stream type and an optional audio_url.

steps.title: Validate the wishes
steps.detail: preferred_file is normalised (lower case, leading dot removed) and must be a supported extension; preferred_type must be audio or video.

steps.title: Complete bare candidates
steps.detail: Only for candidates without an extension: extension from the URL, media kind from the extension, MIME type from EXTENSION_CONTENT_TYPES, download type from the extension (m3u8 → HLS, mpd → DASH, anything supported → FILE).

steps.title: Base score: extension and keywords
steps.detail:
Part of _makeFoundMediaFromUrl, so it only runs for candidates that arrived without an extension and with prio still negative. mp4 100, mkv 95, webm 90, then the audio formats from flac 45 down to mp3 25, and m3u8 and mpd at 20.

Good keywords: master +100, playlist +80, index +70. Bad ones: preview −100, thumbnail −500, ads −1000 — large enough to put those candidates out of reach.

A candidate that arrives complete keeps its prio of −1 and only gains points from the wishes below. Because the winner must beat the initial −1, such a candidate is not picked at all when neither wish matches.

steps.title: Apply the client's wishes
steps.detail: preferred_file is worth more than every other term put together, which is the intent — if the caller asked for mp3, it should get mp3.

branches.label: why this can pick the wrong transport

steps.title: Measure the winner
steps.detail: A Range: bytes=0-0 request per URL; the size comes from Content-Range or Content-Length. With a separate audio URL the total is the sum, or −1 if either is unknown. For HLS the total is always −1, because progress is counted in segments.

steps.title: ProviderResult
steps.sub: url, audio_url, download_type, sizes, mime, extension
steps.detail: The winner, plus an Info block recording what was asked for and what was found. The server turns this into a DownloadContext.

steps.title: The table mixes two levels
steps.detail:
m3u8 and mpd describe how the media is transferred; mp3 and mp4 describe what the target file is. Both sit in one priority table.

So with preferred_file="mp3" a progressive MP3 URL wins on +1000 against an HLS playlist. Worth knowing before adding entries to the table.

steps.title: Nothing usable
steps.detail: An invalid wish raises ArgumentError; a list in which no candidate scored above zero or had a URL raises TaskFailedError with the list of supported extensions.

steps.title: Provider constructs its browser
steps.detail: SoundcloudMediaBrowser, YoutubeMusicMediaBrowser and the new FilmpalastMediaBrowser subclass MediaBrowser. The constructor validates the host before anything launches.

steps.title: Launch Chromium
steps.detail: Synchronous Playwright. headless=False is the common case here because a headful browser gets past more checks — which also means a window really appears on the server machine.

steps.title: Load cookies.txt
steps.sub: Mozilla format, written back on stop
steps.detail: Logins survive across runs this way. The path comes from ROOT_DIR = os.getcwd() evaluated at import time, so starting the server from a different directory silently points at a different file and the login looks lost.

steps.title: Navigate and wait for a player
steps.sub: video, audio, iframe or a div named *player*
steps.detail: A 10 second wait_for_selector that is wrapped in a bare except: pass — if no player appears the run simply continues and relies on the timeout below.

steps.title: Run the configured actions
steps.sub: a list of dicts, in order
steps.detail:
actions is a list, so a sequence works as written: Soundcloud rejects the consent banner and then closes the modal. Supported keys are try_click, click and wait; anything else raises with the list of valid actions.

This used to be a single dict, where duplicate keys collapsed and only the last click survived.

steps.title: Press play
steps.detail: Tries the provider's own selectors first, then the shared PLAY_BUTTON_SELECTORS. Playback is what makes the site request the actual media, which is the entire point of this exercise.

steps.title: Every response is classified
steps.detail:
isMediaResponse() decides from the URL, the content type and Playwright's resource type, filtered through GOOD_MEDIA_KEYWORDS and BAD_MEDIA_KEYWORDS.

Providers override this hook: Soundcloud watches for widevine and the encrypted-HLS markers, YouTube Music reads the itag out of the URL and ranks it with ITAG_PRIORITY.

steps.title: stop() returns what was collected
steps.detail: Cookies are written back and the browser is torn down. _raiseFatalError() is checked at three points during the run, so a DRM detection surfaces as an exception rather than an empty list.

steps.title: Empty? retry
steps.detail:
Both browser providers wrap the run in a retry loop.

YouTube Music now increments its counter, so it gives up after retrys attempts and raises. Soundcloud still does not: in soundcloud_media_information.py, retry stays 0, so the loop can only end through the break that needs a non-empty medialist. If the browser finds nothing this spins forever, launching a visible Chromium every pass, and the TaskFailedError below the loop is unreachable.

steps.title: Candidates handed to the scorer
steps.detail: Because these came from real responses, MIME type and size are often already known and do not have to be guessed from the URL.

steps.title: Non-terminating retry loop
steps.detail: A one-line fix, the same one YouTube Music already has: increment retry in the loop body. Until then, a Soundcloud page whose media the browser cannot see will hang the request instead of failing it.

steps.title: DRMProtectedMediaError
steps.detail: Raised as soon as a response URL contains the encryption markers, rather than letting the run finish and produce nothing. The server maps it to 422, which is how the client can tell „protected“ from „not found“.

steps.title: Fetch the m3u8 as text
steps.detail:
Through asyncio.to_thread because the fetch is synchronous.

This is the fragile step: if resolved_url actually points at a media file rather than a playlist, there is no clean error — you get a decode error from deep inside.

steps.title: dertermineFileType
steps.detail: Decided from the tags present in the text: #EXT-X-STREAM-INF, #EXT-X-I-FRAME-STREAM-INF or #EXT-X-MEDIA mean master; #EXTINF, #EXT-X-TARGETDURATION, #EXT-X-MAP and friends mean index. Text that does not start with #EXTM3U is unknown.

steps.title: Master: choose the variants
steps.detail: Picks the best video variant by bandwidth and looks for a matching audio rendition by language, using preferred_languages when the dispatcher was given one. Both URLs are written back onto context.target (resolved_url and audio_url).

steps.title: Index: build the segment lists
steps.detail:
One IndexHLSDownload for video and, if there is an audio URL, one for audio. Each entry is resolved against its playlist's URL; an #EXT-X-MAP init section becomes a segment with duration 0. total_segments is the sum of both lists.

When the server streams HLS to a player instead, it computes the same two lists up front and caches them on the ServerStream, so its playlist routes are memory lookups.

steps.title: Stream the segments
steps.sub: downloadAndYield, bounded by the download semaphore
steps.detail: Each segment is fetched with asyncDownloadYieldSimple(), honouring its byte range. Progress is updated per chunk (bytes) and per segment.

steps.title: Copy or mux
steps.detail: A master playlist usually separates the streams, so video and audio arrive as two generators and ffmpeg joins them through two input pipes. A single source whose codecs fit the found container is passed through untouched.

steps.title: Byte stream
steps.detail: The stream path is the one in use. _runContextLocal() still calls the pre-rework constructors of MasterHLSDownload and IndexHLSDownload and would fail; the server has LOCAL downloads switched off.

steps.title: TaskFailedError
steps.sub: unknown playlist, no segments, ffmpeg error
steps.detail: The dispatcher marks the context FAILED, stores the message in error_message and re-raises. A missing ffmpeg surfaces as FFmpegNotFoundError instead.

steps.title: Why UMP exists
steps.sub: googlevideo.com does not serve plain ranges
steps.detail:
YouTube delivers through its own container format. Unlike FILE and HLS this protocol is stateful: the server only answers a POST body that says how far the client has already got.

That is why DownloadTarget carries a post_body field at all — it exists solely for this path. Since the YouTube provider resolves direct format URLs and HLS manifests itself, this path is only reached by URLs that still point at googlevideo or a watch page.

steps.title: getUMPMode
steps.detail:
Read from the query string of resolved_url. Anything else raises ValueError("Unknown UMP transport").

In the stream path the sabr branch creates its generator but never iterates it, so it currently sends zero bytes and still reports FINISHED. The ump branch goes through the codec check like FILE and HLS.

steps.title: POST with the current offset
steps.detail: The body is a protobuf message. Rather than build it from scratch, the code patches the offsets into the body captured earlier, which is what sabr_patcher.py isolates.

steps.title: Parse parts out of the byte stream
steps.detail: The only place in the project that parses at byte level. Each part is a varint type, a varint length and a payload; _read_varint / _write_varint are the base unit.

steps.title: Assemble media chunks
steps.detail: Only some part types carry media; the rest are control messages that update the position for the next request.

steps.title: Continue from the new offset
steps.sub: the loop the whole mechanism is built around
steps.detail: The response tells the client where it got to; that offset is patched into the next POST. This repeats until the media is complete — which is why a UMP download cannot simply be resumed with an HTTP range header.

steps.title: Range requests from a player
steps.detail: downloadAndYieldUMPRange() translates a byte range into the offsets this protocol understands. The server's file watch route uses it when a player seeks inside a UMP target.

steps.title: youtube mode: yt-dlp
steps.detail: For a plain watch URL the whole job is handed to yt-dlp as a subprocess: bestaudio or bestvideo+bestaudio, merged by yt-dlp's own ffmpeg call into the found container and written to stdout. This branch skips the engine's codec check. yt-dlp must be on PATH as a command, not only installed as a Python package.
